patch.description_long: In 1953, Senator Joseph McCarthy hired Roy Cohn as chief counsel to the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations. PBS’s American Experience account says McCarthy relied heavily on Cohn for contacts, information, ideas, and political advice. Cohn had recently gained public prominence as a prosecutor in the espionage case against Julius and Ethel Rosenberg. In his new role, he helped McCarthy conduct investigations into alleged communist influence in government and public life during the Red Scare. The committee’s investigations and McCarthy’s tactics became closely associated with the term McCarthyism. Historical accounts describe Cohn as an influential aide, while the available sources do not establish that he invented McCarthyism or acted as its sole architect. This appointment took place decades before Donald Trump’s political career and has no documented connection to him. The event is Cohn’s appointment and influence within McCarthy’s committee, situated in the broader history of the Red Scare.

reason: Removed the false birth chronology: Trump was born in 1946, before Cohn’s 1953 appointment. Also removes review-facing commentary about the title and states the event history directly.

patch.description_long: During the Vietnam-era draft, Donald Trump received four student deferments while studying at Fordham University and the University of Pennsylvania. After graduating in 1968, he received a 1-Y medical deferment. The New York Times reported that Trump said a doctor diagnosed bone spurs in his heels and wrote a letter for his local draft board. Selective Service records obtained from the National Archives do not specify the condition, and Trump could not recall the doctor’s name when asked by the Times. A Selective Service spokesman said Trump was medically exempted before the 1969 draft lottery, so his eventual lottery number did not determine his status. His medical classification later changed to 4-F in 1972. The records document four education deferments and one medical deferment. They do not prove that the diagnosis was fabricated or establish that Trump intended to evade service.

reason: Removes commentary about the original headline and keeps the reported chronology and evidentiary limits in reader-facing form.

patch.description_long: Project 2025 presented a policy program for a possible conservative administration, including proposals affecting technology, media, and communications. Brookings’ analysis describes plans to expand presidential power over agencies and to redirect Federal Trade Commission antitrust enforcement toward what the project’s authors characterize as social and political concerns about Big Tech. The analysis also notes that Project 2025 says little about artificial-intelligence policy and does not set out solutions for privacy, safety, or the information ecosystem. Those proposals do not amount to a comprehensive data-retention system. The linked Brookings and WIRED coverage does not identify a rule compelling companies to retain all communications, browsing records, or location data, specify a retention period, or create blanket government access. Nor do those sources establish encryption backdoors or warrantless surveillance infrastructure. The documented policy debate concerns proposed agency and enforcement changes, alongside significant gaps in the plan’s treatment of privacy and AI.

reason: Removes review-facing references to the previous description and keeps the distinction between proposals and unsupported implementation claims.

patch.description_long: On September 29, 1993, Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell attended a White House event for donors to a restoration project. Photographs taken by White House photographer Ralph Alswang show them speaking with President Bill Clinton after he delivered remarks. The gathering documents that Epstein and Maxwell attended a presidential event and met Clinton in that setting. It predates the criminal cases that later brought Epstein’s abuse into public view. A photograph of a brief conversation does not establish what Clinton knew about Epstein or his later conduct, and it is not evidence that Clinton participated in abuse. The photographs concern an event at the Clinton White House; they do not identify Donald Trump as a participant. They provide a record of Epstein and Maxwell’s presence at a political and donor gathering, while leaving the nature and significance of their interaction with Clinton undocumented.
